claims.citation: New York Herald, 17 July 1866, p. 8, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Atlantic, Hover, Bremen June 28, and South-
ampton July 2, with mdse and 1020 passengers, to Ruger
Bros. Experienced strong head winds the greater part of
the passage. July 8, lat 36[?] 47, lon 29 30, passed ship Reso-
lute, bound E; same date, lat 46 31, lon 30, ship Origine
(Ham), bound E; 12th, lat 42 44, lon 53 10, a National Co's
steamer; 13th, lat 42 36, lon —, bark Baltimore (Prus), bound
W; 14th, ship Scotia, bound E; 15th, off Nantucket, four out-
ward bound steamers.

Steamship Atlantic, Hager, Bremen June 29[?] and Southampton
July 2, with mdse. and 1,020 pass. to Ruger Bros. Experienced strong
head winds the greater part of the passage. July 8, in lat. 46 37 N,
long. 29 30 W, passed American ship Resolute[?], bound E; July 12, in
lat. 42 44 N, long. 53 10, passed a steamship of the National Steamship
Co.; July 14, in lat. 40 56, long. 67 40, passed American ship Scotia,
bound E; July 15, off Nantucket, passed four outward bound steamer.
